name: Jehoiachin
description: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy

points: Jehoiakim slept with his fathers and Jehoiachin his son reigned in his place.

note.label: 2 Kings 24: Judah Carried Away for the Sins of Manasseh

points: Jehoiachin was eighteen years old and reigned three months in Jerusalem, and did evil in the sight of the Lord according to all his fathers had done.

note.label: 2 Kings 24: Judah Carried Away for the Sins of Manasseh

points: Jehoiachin went out to the king of Babylon with his mother, servants, princes, and officers, and the king of Babylon took him in the eighth year of his reign.

note.label: 2 Kings 24: Judah Carried Away for the Sins of Manasseh

points: Jehoiakim's son Jehoiachin reigned three months, did evil, went out to Nebuchadnezzar and was taken in the eighth year of his reign with his mother, his wives, his officers and the mighty of the land.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

points: And he carried away Jehoiachin to Babylon, and the king's mother, and the king's wives, and his officers, and the mighty of the land, those carried he into captivity from Jerusalem to Babylon.

note.label: Israel Called Gentiles, Strangers, Heathen & Saints

points: He carried Jehoiachin, the king's mother, wives, and officers to Babylon, along with the men of might and craftsmen and smiths, wanting them to build for him what they had built in their own land, as conquering nations always used Israel's skill and industry.

note.label: 2 Kings 24: Judah Carried Away for the Sins of Manasseh

points: In the thirty seventh year of the captivity of Jehoiachin, Evilmerodach king of Babylon lifted up his head out of prison and spake kindly to him.

note.label: 2 Kings 25: The Fall of Jerusalem and the Burning of the Temple

points: The sons of Jeconiah were Assir and Salathiel, and Salathiel's brothers included Pedaiah; whether Assir is a name or a title for the captive makes no difference to the line.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

points: The sons of Jeconiah are named, and the line is carried through Salathiel, Pedaiah, and Zerubbabel after the captivity.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 3: The Sons of David and the Kings of Judah

points: Jehoiachin is eight years old when he begins to reign and reigns three months and ten days in Jerusalem, and he does that which is evil in the sight of the Lord.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 36: The Captivity of Judah into Babylon

points: There was a certain Jew in Shushan named Mordecai, son of Jair, a Benjamite carried away from Jerusalem with the captivity taken with Jeconiah king of Judah whom Nebuchadnezzar carried away. This gives the lapse of time telling when Mordecai was put into captivity.

note.label: Esther 2: Esther Made Queen and Mordecai Uncovers the Plot

points: The people are told not to weep for the dead but to weep sore for him that goes away, Shallum the son of Josiah who reigned in his father's place.
Shallum went forth out of his place and shall not return, but shall die in the land where they led him captive and see his native country no more.

note.label: Jeremiah 22: Woe to the Unrighteous Kings of Judah

points: Two baskets of figs before the temple after Jeconiah was carried to Babylon: one very good, the other so naughty they could not be eaten.

note.label: The Mercy and Humility of King Manasseh

points: The Most High shows Jeremiah two baskets of figs set before the temple after Nebuchadnezzar had carried Jeconiah, the princes of Judah, the carpenters, and the smiths away captive to Babylon.

note.label: Jeremiah 24: The Two Baskets of Figs

points: King Zedekiah the son of Josiah reigns in place of Coniah, whom Nebuchadnezzar made king in the land of Judah, but neither he nor his servants nor the people hearken to the words of the Most High spoken by Jeremiah.

note.label: Jeremiah 37: The Prophet Arrested and Imprisoned

points: In the thirty-seventh year of the captivity of Jehoiachin king of Judah, Evilmerodach king of Babylon in the first year of his reign lifted up his head, brought him out of prison, and spake kindly to him.
Jehoiachin was the real king carried captive earlier in Second Kings 24, and after his long imprisonment he found favor; his lineage became the line through which Christ came.

note.label: Jeremiah 52: The Fall of Jerusalem and the Puppet King Zedekiah

points: After they were brought to Babylon, Jechonias begat Salathiel and Salathiel begat Zorobabel, both in captivity; a captive does not sit on the throne.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

points: From the sit down: one of the pastors said there was a curse on Jeconiah that nobody of his seed would sit as king, so the genealogy is ruled out. Think: after Jeconiah, was there a king in Israel sitting on the throne? No. When Babylon came in, that was it; Zedekiah came, and they killed him with his sons. There was no king during the time of Christ, because the prophets said there would be no more king until Christ returns.

cases.name: Jehoahaz (Shallum) of Judah
cases.charge: Doing evil in the sight of the Lord according to all that his fathers had done
cases.preview: After Josiah fell at Megiddo the people of the land anointed his son Jehoahaz, called Shallum, and in three months he did evil according to all his fathers had done (2 Kings 23:30-32).

cases.name: Jehoiachin (Coniah)
cases.charge: Doing evil as his father Jehoiakim had done; a signet plucked from the Lord’s right hand
cases.preview: Jehoiachin, called Coniah and Jeconiah, reigned three months and did evil as his father Jehoiakim had done (2 Kings 24:8-9).
